neighbours.label: Coulomb and electrostatic vocabulary (cou|l|omb, Coul|omb, electro|static, ' rep' in repulsive)
fire: An electron carries a charge of 1.6 x 10-19 coulombs.
Coulomb's law gives the electric force between ions.
Electrostatic repulsion keeps the charged spheres apart.
The electrostatic precipitator removes dust from the flue gas.
Measuring coulombs of charge is the basis of the method.
The Coulomb force falls off with the square of the distance.
Electrostatic attraction holds the salt crystal together.
This capacitor stores a few coulombs at high voltage.
quiet: An electron has a mass of 9.1 x 10-31 kilograms.
Newton's law gives the gravity between planets.
Strong magnets keep the iron spheres in place.
The steel filter removes dust from the flue gas.
Measuring grams of metal is the basis of the method.
The tidal force falls off with the cube of the distance.
Hydrogen bonding holds the water molecules together.
This battery stores a few kilowatts at low voltage.

notes: Card: ' rep' x5, 'l' x3, ' Coul' x3, 'omb' x2, 'static' x2, ' capacitor' x2. Probes: 'l' in coulombs 0.897, 'static' 0.665, 'l' in coulometric 0.469, 'omb' 0.411; 'dollars' 0.008, 'Newton's law' 0.063. Near misses keep physics without this vocabulary. Tokens are checked.
